research_rationale:
EO 10860 (25 FR 1089, signed 1960-02-05; held official Federal Register text) prescribes the design of the Coat of Arms of the President of the United States (section 1), the Seal of the President (section 2), the Color and Flag of the President (section 3), makes the accompanying illustrations and specifications part of the order and reserves the designs to represent the President exclusively (section 4), and in section 5 fixes its effective date as July 4, 1960 and supersedes Executive Order No. 10823 of May 26, 1959 as of that date. The dossier inventory had four rows, ran sections 2 and 3 together and omitted section 3 (the held OCR prints the heading as 'Sec.. 3.'); five inventory overrides cut from the held text correct this, one per section. Sections 1 to 4 contain no term, condition or sunset. Section 5 is spent: the order took effect and EO 10823 was superseded on its stated date, 1960-07-04, which is the first end of that clause by the order's own text. The packet carries no later instrument that amends, revokes or supersedes EO 10860 (later-events chain empty; the OFR catalog search and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches record no hit naming the order), and the held texts that cite the number are the order itself and its adjacent Federal Register text. Sections 1 to 4 are therefore carried as operative on the order's own held text with no end, read with the bounded searches. Limit stated plainly: no held current-law source positively cites EO 10860, so the continuation rests on the absence of any ending instrument and the order's own text, which fixes standing designs with no term.
